target_customer: Beginner investors, originally teens and later 18 to 25 year olds, who pay a monthly or annual fee
problem: Young people want to invest but lack financial knowledge, so Bloom pairs interactive lessons and rewards with a brokerage account.
business_model: Consumer subscription (15 dollars per month or 120 dollars per year per TechCrunch 2023)
product_category: Investing education app with brokerage account

founders.name: Sam Yang
previous_startups: AI based photo app with over 250,000 users
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says Yang took Bloom through YC W21. YC bio says he later started Nova Software.

founders.name: Allan Maman
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch July 2023; not on the YC page text.

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app with brokerage integration and compliance requirements. Content and gamification were standard, brokerage and regulation added effort.

defensibility.rationale: Lesson content and gamification are copyable. Regulatory registration as an adviser and a young user base helped modestly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Greenlight and Copper are named as competitors in 2023 coverage.

market_need_then: Retail investing surged in 2020 and 2021 and young users sought education. Claimed 1 million downloads within about a year of launch (TechCrunch, July 2023).

identity.mascot_or_character: AI assistant called Bloomie and in app currency called Oinks, per the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Approachable, no jargon, investing made easy

branding.brand_signature: Oinks rewards currency and Bloomie assistant
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in TechCrunch, Fast Company and Benzinga; site claims 2 million downloads and 80K monthly investors. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Playful brand elements and press coverage, but a very common name that collides with many Bloom products. Download figures are company claims.

pivots.from: Teens aged 13 and up as main users
pivots.to: Users aged 18 to 25 as nearly three quarters of the base
pivots.why: User base shifted per TechCrunch; not a stated pivot.

outcome_analysis: Bloom launched in February 2022, reported 1 million downloads and seven figure annual recurring revenue by mid 2023, and is still active with claims of 2 million downloads. Total disclosed funding is about 4.4 million dollars in seed. It has not raised a larger round or exited in sources found, so it looks like a modest consumer fintech.
notes: Seed total is 4.4 million dollars announced July 2023 by TechCrunch and Contrary, much of it raised in 2022, so the date 2022 is approximate. One 2022 report cited 3.3 million dollars; the CB Insights 500 thousand dollar convertible note (Jan 2021) and the 125 thousand dollar YC entry are aggregator only and unverified. YC page says launched April 2022 and over 1 million users, TechCrunch says February 2022. Competitors Copper and Greenlight appear in a 2023 source only, so no competitor is listed under the as of 2021 rule. Founded year 2021 is from an aggregator profile.
